entries.final_answer: Answered from #7755/#7754 (unattended scheduled run): the operator running spec-kitty consolidate on a lanes Mission whose approved lanes edit the same file; the in-run auto-rebase of the later lane stops on a conflict with a sibling lane consolidated earlier in that run; the rollback then restores the Mission branch. The refusal must say the auto-rebase stopped and why, name the sibling lane branch (it survives rollback), and give a remedy that works for an approved WP; after the operator follows it, the next run must pass the lane.
entries.question: Who hits the stale refusal, when, and what must happen next?

entries.final_answer: Reopen the WP (move-task --to planned --review-feedback-file, costs a re-review), re-enter it with agent action implement (names the lane checkout), merge the named sibling lane branch there and resolve, commit, hand back for review and approval, re-run consolidate. Verified end to end in an exploratory run: the next consolidate passes the lane and reconciliation verifies. A refusal with no sibling lane keeps the implement auto-rebase refresh, preceded by the reopen step (#7754).
entries.question: Which recovery route does the refusal prescribe for an approved work package?

entries.final_answer: No. Rollback semantics, the single rollback authority, CAS discipline and the approved-bound refusals stay unchanged; the fix is diagnostic and remedy text only. Dry-run forecasting of this refusal (#7324) and the reconciliation attribution of unreviewed merges (#5604/#5053) stay out of scope.
